chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Auditioning for Charlie Johnson; Kenneth Roane; Local 802 card
summary: Kenneth Roane vouched for him to Charlie Johnson, and Mr. Small had him taken to Local 802 for a union card.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: We were going to -- you were starting to talk about Charlie Johnson.

Charlie Johnson, yeah. So little things like that, picked up a couple of dollars, kept me eating. So I went down to Charlie Johnson's, and I had met Ham Davis, who's a trumpet player. I had met Charlie. Oh, drummer, uh, I'll recall his name in a minute. One of the greatest guys -- uh, I -- oh, what, what, what,what? Trying to think. Oh, Roane-- Kenneth Roane was the trumpet player in the band. He was a very fine man. When he -- I still say he's one of the greatest trumpet players that ever came to New York, ever around New York, and arrangers, and all that, because I played a lot of his music. You ever see any of Ken-
Beautiful! It looks like a picture.

I mean when he sits down and writes it's -- he's a perfectionist, playing, and writing, and when he's -- back when I first with him, years ago, I mean playing, I mean anyway, he's -- I still love him. He's a great guy.
My man playing drums, I can't remember.
I -- anyway, I went down to see him, Kenneth told me, come in, sit down. And he heard me play. Kenneth say play this for me, or play that for me. I played. He told Charlie I was all right.
So, Charlie said okay fellow, you in the band. And meantime, Mr. Smalls, [crossed out], called this guy up, and said pick him up, [crossed out] Jimmy, take him down to 802 and give him a card.
Oh, you didn't have your card then.

No, I wasn't -- no. They took me down to 802 and got me a card and put me in the union, and back that time -- so it was easy. I was a union man. I was in the union, I had an 802 card in my pocket, and a job.
